# Right Sidebar Scope

## How To Build

A RightSidebarScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A RightSidebarScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Side

right

## Width

260

## Min Width

160

## Panels

- [ReferencedFilesPanel](./index.md#referenced-files-panel)
- [UnderstandingPanel](./index.md#understanding-panel)

## Sidebar

It runs along the right of what it sits beside, with a thin line down its left edge, where the two meet. It is resized by dragging that edge: it starts 260 pixels wide and can't be dragged narrower than 160.
It holds its panels one above the other, in the order it lists them, each across its full width. A single thin line, in the theme's line colour, lies between one panel and the next, never two, unless the next panel says its own change of colour is the edge. A panel that isn't shown for the moment takes no room and leaves no line.
It is on the theme's base surface, as its panels' bodies are.

## Concept

### Pitch

A second [SidebarScope](../sidebar/index.md#sidebar-scope), at the right of the message list and the chat input beneath it, that lists the spec files the running task references, so it's clear what part of the spec the harness is working from, and the constraints it has taken from it for the task.

### Shape

#### Description

It runs the full height of the body, beside the body's tab bar, the message list or file beneath it, and the chat input beneath those, which stops at its left edge rather than running beneath it. It keeps the width it was dragged to while the application runs.
Its two panels, the referenced files above the understanding, sit one above the other: the referenced files only as tall as their rows need, up to half the sidebar's height, scrolling beyond that, and the understanding filling the rest.

#### Look

The sidebar's body is on the ribbon's command area colour, #222222 in dark mode. Each panel's header is 32 pixels tall, on the darkest surface, #111111 in dark mode, as the file tree is, its title in small semibold text, 8 pixels from the left, with no count beside it. There is no line anywhere in it, not between a header and its body, nor between one panel and the next: the change of colour is the edge. The only line is the one down its left edge, where it meets the message list and the chat input, which is the handle it is resized by. In light mode the same steps are taken, as the ribbon's are.
Neither panel has a permanent scrollbar, since its column would break the 8 pixel inset: a panel shows its scrollbar only while its contents are taller than it, and none otherwise. When it shows, it is the same scrollbar as every other, as the [ScrollbarScope](../scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope) says.
A panel whose contents fit doesn't scroll at all, not even by a pixel, at any display scale or window size: it counts as taller than its contents need only once they overflow it by a whole pixel or more, so what is left over from rounding to the display's pixels never counts, and while they fit, it stays scrolled to its top. So neither the wheel nor a drag moves rows that all fit, and no scrollbar shows for them.

#### Showing

It is only there while a task is running: from the moment a task is sent from the Code, Chain, or Spec tab until its run is over. Questions from the Ask tab never show it, even when one is sent from the queue.
When a task starts, it slides out from the right edge of the message list and the chat input, growing from nothing to its width, its contents sliding into view from behind that edge as it does. When the run is over, it slides back the same way. The slide is quick and settles without bouncing. The message list and the chat input take the rest of the width, laid out anew only once the slide settles.

# Referenced Files Panel

## How To Build

A ReferencedFilesPanel should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A ReferencedFilesPanel should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Title

Referenced Spec

## Counted

false

## Height

fit

## Scrolls

true

## Scrollbar

overflowing

## Panel

It has a header along its top, reading its title in small, semibold text, with a little padding around it. The header is on the theme's raised surface and the panel's body on its base surface, so the header stands slightly apart from the body, contrasting with it only a little, with no line between them.
It shows no count of what it lists.
It is only as tall as its contents need, taking no more of its sidebar's height.
Its contents scroll on their own when they are taller than it, with a scrollbar along its right only while they are, as the ScrollbarScope says; while they fit, it has no scrollbar and doesn't scroll at all.

## Concept

### Pitch

The top panel of the [RightSidebarScope](./index.md#right-sidebar-scope): the spec files the running task references.

### Shape

#### Description

One row per spec file the running task references, each listed once: first those its prompt imports from, then the rest in the order they are first referenced. The rows sit 8 pixels in from the panel's edges, above and below as well as at the sides, each 24 pixels tall, with no icon: each shows its file name alone, in small text, without its folders, cut off with an ellipsis when the sidebar is too narrow, its full path in its tooltip. A file named index, whatever its extension, such as `index.pi`, shows the folder it is in before its name, as `chat-input/index.pi`, and no folder above that.

#### Referencing

A spec file is one in the spec location, as the [ProjectLocationsScope](../../../scope/project-locations/index.md#project-locations-scope) says; a compiled spec file is one under `.claude/reference`, which stands for part of the spec. Both are listed, and files anywhere else are not. A file's full path counts however long it is, and a relative path is read from the project directory.
A file is referenced, however the harness reads it, when:

- the task's prompt imports from it, its hidden anchor naming it
- the harness reads, edits, or writes it with a file tool
- a shell command reads it, such as cat, head, tail, sed, less, grep, rg, awk, or diff naming it, or a pattern or folder that takes it in, as far as the command shows
- a shell command edits or writes it, such as sed -i, a redirect (> or >>), tee, mv, or cp onto it
- a search tool, Grep or Glob, searches a folder or pattern that takes it in and its results name it
- a subagent the harness starts does any of the above

A file taken in only by a folder or pattern, without the results naming it, is not listed. A command whose target can't be worked out is skipped rather than guessed at. A file referenced again isn't listed again.
A file edited or written in any of these ways, rather than only read or imported, shows a small pencil icon at the right of its row. A row a subagent referenced shows the same way, with "Read by a subagent" in its tooltip beneath its full path.
Clicking a row opens its file, as the [OpenFileScope](../../../scope/open-file/index.md#open-file-scope) says. While no spec file is referenced yet, the list reads "No spec files referenced yet", muted.

A UnderstandingPanel should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

## Title

Understanding

## Counted

false

## Height

fill

## Scrolls

true

## Scrollbar

overflowing

## Panel

It has a header along its top, reading its title in small, semibold text, with a little padding around it. The header is on the theme's raised surface and the panel's body on its base surface, so the header stands slightly apart from the body, contrasting with it only a little, with no line between them.
It shows no count of what it lists.
It fills the height its sidebar's other panels leave.
Its contents scroll on their own when they are taller than it, with a scrollbar along its right only while they are, as the ScrollbarScope says; while they fit, it has no scrollbar and doesn't scroll at all.

## Concept

### Pitch

The bottom panel of the [RightSidebarScope](./index.md#right-sidebar-scope): the constraints the harness has taken from the spec for the running task.

### Shape

#### Description

It shows the running task's understanding file, as the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](../../../scope/prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope) says, as it is written: one row per item of its Markdown list, in the file's order, its text wrapping rather than cut off. Each row is a box on the ribbon's tab row colour, #333333 in dark mode, with corners rounded 4 pixels, its text in small text with a 20 pixel line height, 8 pixels of padding either side and 6 above and below, so it is 32 pixels tall for a single line; the boxes sit 8 pixels in from the panel's edges and 4 pixels apart. Anything in the file that isn't a list item is left out.
A row's text is its item's, with any link shown as its text alone. Clicking a row opens the file its link points to, read from the project directory, as the [OpenFileScope](../../../scope/open-file/index.md#open-file-scope) says. A row whose link points to a file that doesn't exist shows its text muted, and clicking it does nothing; a row with no link does nothing either.
It follows the file as it changes on disk while the task runs. A row that is added, or whose text changes, is briefly highlighted, fading back to its box's colour. Until the file exists, it reads "Nothing understood yet", muted. Once it exists but has no list items yet, as when it has just been created, the panel shows nothing beneath its header, and has nothing to scroll and no scrollbar.

content.text:
The right sidebar now waits until the running task has something to show before it slides out. I haven't opened the app to watch it.

- **What counts as something to show:** a spec file the task has referenced, at least one constraint in its understanding file, or a subagent it has started. Until one of those arrives, nothing slides out and the message list and chat input keep the full width.
- **Once it's out, it stays out until the run ends,** then slides back as before. So a brief moment with nothing in it (for example, the understanding file being rewritten) won't make it flicker in and out.
- **Everything else is unchanged:** Ask-tab questions still never show it, and the slide animation is the same. Switching projects also follows the new rule: a project whose running task has nothing to show yet doesn't show the sidebar.

The change is in `refs_wanted` in `src/prompt_mode.rs`, plus a new `refs_have_contents` check.

**Tests:** `referenced_spec_shows_the_understanding` expected the sidebar to be there while still empty, which is exactly what you asked to change. I updated it to check that the sidebar stays in until the understanding file has items, and that it's out once they appear. All 5 referenced-spec tests pass.

The full suite still has 6 failures:
- **Four seen in earlier turns:** the three prompt-wording tests (in `hidden_anchor.rs` and `system_prompts.rs`) and `code_tasks_sent_to_spec_are_told_what_the_code_task_did`.
- **`selected_answer_text_can_be_copied_or_attached`:** it also failed two turns ago and passed when run on its own then.
- **`referenced_spec_shows_the_understanding`:** this is the test I then fixed. I didn't rerun the full suite after that fix.

The spec's "Showing" section still says the sidebar slides out the moment a task starts, so it will need updating to match. This turn's constraints are in `.suspense/history/1790707288-Prompt_d1542e39e7a2caa8.understanding.md`.
